title: Generators and eventual kernel capture identify a restricted module colimit
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and $(M_i,f_{ij})_{i\in I}$ a directed system of $R$-modules. Let compatible linear maps $u_i:M_i\to M$ exhibit $M$ as its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $J\subseteq I$ be nonempty and directed in its inherited order. Assume there is a subset $E\subseteq M$ whose finite $R$-linear combinations exhaust $M$, and for every $x\in E$ there are $i\in J$ and $y\in M_i$ with $u_i(y)=x$. Assume also that for every $i\in J$ there is $j\in J$ with $j\ge i$ such that $\ker(f_{ik})\subseteq\ker(f_{ij})$ for every $k\in I$ with $k\ge i$. Then the canonical linear map $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in J}M_i\to M$ induced by the restricted cocone is an isomorphism. No countability, finite-presentation, injectivity of transitions, or Mittag-Leffler hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 059W (lemma-ML-countable-colimit), proof, the final two paragraphs; extracted general restricted-colimit criterion from properties (2) and the kernel inclusion in (3).

proof.text: The inherited index category $J$ is small, nonempty and filtered, since it is a directed subposet of the small poset $I$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The maps $u_i$ for $i\in J$ form a cocone. For $m\in M$, write $m=\sum_{a=1}^n r_a x_a$ with $x_a\in E$. Choose $i_a\in J$ and $y_a\in M_{i_a}$ representing each $x_a$. Repeated use of directedness gives $h\in J$ above all $i_a$; when $n=0$, choose any $h\in J$. Linearity and compatibility give $u_h(\sum_{a=1}^n r_a f_{i_a h}(y_a))=\sum_{a=1}^n r_a u_{i_a}(y_a)=m$. Thus every element of $M$ is represented by one stage in $J$.

source.place: Tag 059W, lemma-ML-countable-colimit, proof, final paragraph after properties (1)–(3).

proof.text: Fix $i\in J$ and $z\in M_i$ with $u_i(z)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] to the given colimit over the small filtered category $I$: there is $k\in I$, $k\ge i$, with $f_{ik}(z)=0$. Choose the $j\in J$, $j\ge i$, in the kernel-capture hypothesis. Its inclusion $\ker(f_{ik})\subseteq\ker(f_{ij})$ implies $f_{ij}(z)=0$. This gives eventual vanishing inside $J$; it does not require $j\ge k$.

source.place: Tag 059W, lemma-ML-countable-colimit, proof, final paragraph after properties (1)–(3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] to the restricted diagram over $J$ and cocone $(M,(u_i)_{i\in J})$. Step 1 verifies its representative condition and all index and cocone hypotheses. For its equality condition, if $u_i(x)=u_i(y)$, apply Step 2 to $z=x-y$; then $f_{ij}(x-y)=0$ gives $f_{ij}(x)=f_{ij}(y)$ by linearity. Hence this restricted cocone is a colimit in $R$-modules.

source.place: Tag 059W, lemma-ML-countable-colimit, proof, final paragraph after properties (1)–(3).

proof.text: Let $L=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in J}M_i$ with legs $v_i$, and let $a:L\to M$ be the canonical map, so $av_i=u_i$. Since Step 3 makes $M$ another colimit of the same diagram, its universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $b:M\to L$ with $bu_i=v_i$. Then $(ab)u_i=u_i$ and $(ba)v_i=v_i$ for every $i\in J$. Uniqueness in the two universal properties yields $ab=1_M$ and $ba=1_L$. Thus the specified canonical map $a$ is an isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem isIso_restrictedColimit_of_generators_kernel_capture (R : Type u) [CommRing R] {I : Type v} [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c) (J : Set I) [Nonempty J] [IsDirected J (· ≤ ·)] (E : Set c.pt) (hspan : Submodule.span R E = ⊤) (hrepresent : ∀ x ∈ E, ∃ (i : J) (y : F.obj i.val), c.ι.app i.val y = x) (hkernel : ∀ i : J, ∃ (j : J) (hij : i.val ≤ j.val), ∀ (k : I) (hik : i.val ≤ k), LinearMap.ker (F.map (homOfLE hik)).hom ≤ LinearMap.ker (F.map (homOfLE hij)).hom) : IsIso (colimit.desc ((Subtype.mono_coe (· ∈ J)).functor ⋙ F) (c.whisker (Subtype.mono_coe (· ∈ J)).functor))
